frozen_scientific_scope.geology: Lower Carboniferous Limestone, Gilmerton, Scotland, for P3317 plate record.

scale.method: Plate XII Fig1 is printed one-third natural size. Its approximately 950 px horizontal span in rendered page686 at 2200px height / page height562.6pt yields approximately 0.257m after 3x scaling. Check against Fig3 clavicle on companion plate, stated 0.32m in text, suggests similar order. Round to 0.27m and disclose scan/plate uncertainty approximately 10–15%; thickness is a separate artistic estimate from narrow-jaw description.
scale.prohibition: Do not label 0.27m an exact museum measurement; do not substitute dimensions from the St Andrews slab or isolated 0.17m tusk from different specimens.

frozen_scientific_scope.scope: Preserved single deep, narrow left lower-jaw ramus study. No full fish, upper skull, opposite mirrored ramus or soft tissue. Retain broken/missing zones rather than inventing a pristine complete jaw.
frozen_scientific_scope.specimen_reference: NHM P3317, left mandibular ramus, Woodward catalogue Plate XII Fig1
uncertainties: P3317 external plate supplies preserved silhouette, not all internal surfaces. Modern Rhizodus text supports internal structural interpretation, not exact P3317 measured interior.
Thickness and internal relief are restrained artistic interpretation and must be disclosed. No exact replica/scan claims.
Modern primary full text read; its photographic PDF/image endpoints returned403, so those images were NOT inspected. Historic Plate XII Fig1 was inspected directly and is the frozen visual authority.
Do not add missing third coronoid fang solely because complete species jaw has three coronoids; preserve plate-supported segment.
